evals.prompt:
Help me organize my meeting notes into my journal.

Meeting: Weekly Sync
Start: Feb 27, 2026 at 11:00 AM
End: 11:30 AM
Duration: 30 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: sarah.chen@acme.com, j.rivera-contractor@acme.com, sarah.chen@acme.com

Raw notes:
- discussed Q3 budget overrun
- need to email finance about the discrepancy
- also should schedule a follow-up with the vendor about pricing

Please interview me about each line, then propose creating Trello tasks for the two action items when you're done. I'll answer your questions as we go and confirm everything before you create any cards.
evals.expected_output: The skill establishes metadata (Step 2, no time-mismatch correction needed since 11:00-11:30 already equals the stated 30-minute duration), formats attendees (Step 3: 'Sarah Chen' and 'J. Rivera', title-cased, '-contractor' stripped, deduplicated, alphabetically sorted -- there are only two distinct attendees since sarah.chen@acme.com appears twice), then interviews the user line-by-line (Step 4, one question per line, not batched) before normalizing and bulleting the notes. After staged approval of metadata/attendees/notes, it identifies two action items (email finance about the budget discrepancy; schedule a vendor follow-up about pricing), presents them for confirmation, then asks whether to create Trello tasks. Since the user confirms yes, it calls create-trello-task.sh once per action item with the actual action-item text and a --desc including the meeting title and date, and replaces each checklist item's text with a Markdown link to the returned card URL in the final document.
expectations: Attendees are formatted as 'Sarah Chen' and 'J. Rivera' (title case, -contractor stripped), deduplicated to two people despite the duplicate email, sorted alphabetically by first name.

The transcript shows a genuine per-line interview (at least one clarifying question per raw note line) before the notes are finalized as complete sentences -- the skill does not fabricate finished notes without first asking about each line.
Exactly two create-trello-task.sh invocations occur (one per confirmed action item), each with --desc including the meeting title 'Weekly Sync' and a February 2026 date.
The final Markdown document's Action Items section links each item as `- [ ] [<text>](<trello card url>)` using the exact URLs the fixture returned, not fabricated URLs.
The final document's section order is exactly: metadata block, ###### Attendees, ###### Notes, ###### Action Items, matching Step 8.

Per Step 7.5 ('It is valid for a meeting to have no action items'), it explicitly confirms this with the user rather than fabricating one to have something to show, and per Step 7.8 skips Trello creation entirely since there are no confirmed action items -- it must not call create-trello-task.sh even speculatively.
expectations: Zero create-trello-task.sh invocations occur.
The transcript explicitly confirms with the user that there are no action items, rather than silently omitting the section or inventing one.

evals.prompt:
Organize my notes from today's vendor call.

Meeting: Vendor Call - Acme Supplies
Start: Mar 10, 2026 at 1:00 PM
End: 1:20 PM
Duration: 20 minutes
Attendees: me, rep@acmesupplies.com

Raw notes:
- vendor confirmed new pricing takes effect next quarter
- I need to update our internal pricing sheet before then
- also need to loop in procurement about the change

Interview me about each line, then go ahead and create Trello cards for both action items once we've confirmed them -- I approve that upfront.
evals.expected_output: The skill interviews the user, confirms two action items (update the internal pricing sheet; loop in procurement), and per the user's upfront approval proceeds to create Trello tasks for both. In this scenario, the fixture is set up so the first create-trello-task.sh call succeeds but the second fails (simulating a real API error). The skill must not fabricate a card URL for the failed item, must not silently drop it from the final document, and must clearly surface the failure to the user rather than presenting a broken or misleading final document.
expectations: Exactly two create-trello-task.sh invocations are attempted, one per confirmed action item.
The action item whose call succeeded is linked in the final document using the exact fixture-returned URL.

The action item whose call failed is NOT given a fabricated or guessed URL -- it either remains a plain unlinked checklist item with the failure surfaced to the user, or the skill pauses and asks how to proceed before finalizing that item.
The transcript explicitly reports the create-trello-task.sh failure (e.g. its error message) rather than silently treating it as a success or omitting it from the report.

Nguyen' (title case, -contractor stripped, alphabetical), with Kim Park struck through since she did not attend (the user states this explicitly, distinct from the invited-attendees list). Kim Park's name appears with strikethrough formatting in the final Attendees section, since the user stated she did not attend despite being invited.
